searches.description: Find Ortholog Groups that contain a specified number of proteins. To get Core Groups with peripheral proteins mapped in, choose >=1 for Min/Max Number of Core Proteins and >=1 for Min/Max Core Peripheral Proteins. To get Core Groups with NO peripheral proteins mapped in, choose >=1 for Min/Max Number of Core Proteins and 0 for Min/Max Number of Peripheral Proteins. To get Residual Groups, choose 0 for Min/Max Number of Core Proteins and >=1 for Min/Max Number of Peripheral Proteins. To restrict the total size of the group, set the Number of All Proteins. For example, setting a range of 2 to 499 for Number of All Proteins will show groups for which a cluster graph has been calculated.

groups.description: OrthoMCL contains two sets of genomes. A Core set of 150 genomes have been chosen as well annotated reference organisms that broadly represent the major branches of the tree of life. All of the additional non-core VEuPathDB organisms (pathogens, hosts, and vectors) are called Peripheral organisms, in some cases including multiple strains and genome assemblies for the same species. The search ranges below can be used to filter the number of proteins {taxa} in each orthogroup by the number of Core and Peripheral  (minimum and maximum) in each group.  The number of Core and Peripheral will sum to the number of all proteins {taxa} in the group.

searches.description:
Configure the search to find Ortholog Groups that contain a specified number of Core taxa and Peripheral taxa. For each number, the first box represents the minimum (min) number and the second box represents the maximum (max) number.

  • The Number of All Taxa can be restricted to a range of your choice by inputting numbers into the min and max boxes.
  • To get core groups with peripheral proteins mapped in, input
    • Number of Core Taxa: min=1 and max=150
    • Number of Peripheral Taxa: min=1 and max=700
  • To get core groups with NO peripheral proteins mapped in, input
    • Number of Core Taxa: min=1 and max=150
    • Number of Peripheral Taxa: min=0 and max=0
  • To get residual groups, input
    • Number of Core Taxa: min=0 and max=0
    • Number of Peripheral Taxa: min=1 and max=700

searches.description: Identify ortholog groups based on the median percent identity of all protein sequences within each group. Median percent identity serves as an indicator of group cohesiveness: higher values suggest a tightly clustered group with minimal outliers, while lower values indicate a more dispersed group. Percent identity is represented in decimal form and ranges from 0 to 1 (the equivalent of 0% to 100%). For example, setting the percent identity threshold between 0.8 and 1 will return ortholog groups with a median percent identity between 80% and 100%.

searches.description:
Find Ortholog Groups by phyletic pattern.

Phyletic Pattern Expression is a flexible and powerful way to identify ortholog groups with a certain conservation pattern. The pattern is used to identify groups based on whether proteins from specific taxa are present or absent. Also, the pattern finds groups with a certain copy number (e.g., duplications) within specified taxa.

Examples

These expressions find ortholog groups in which...
hsap>=5there are five or more human sequences
hsap+ecol=2Tboth human and E. coli are present.
hsap+ecol=1Tonly one species of human or E. coli is present.
hsap+ecol>=1Tonly one or both species of human and E. coli is present.
hsap+ecol>=10there are 10 or more human or E. Coli sequences.
EUKA=5there are exactly eukaryotic 5 sequences
EUKA=5Tthere are exactly eukaryotic 5 taxa
hsap+FIRM=2Tthere are exactly 2 human or Gram-positive bacteria taxa
EUKA=35Tthere are all 35 eukaryotic species, ie, Eukaryota-universal groups
EUKA>=5T AND hsap>=10there are at least five eukaryotic species and containing at least 10 human sequences.
(EUKA>=5T AND hsap>=10) OR pfal<20there are at least five eukaryotic species and containing at least 10 human sequences, or there are less than 20 P. falciparum sequences.
ALL=564Tthere are 564 OrthoMCL species. (click on ALL in the graphical display to get up-to-date total number.

Tips

  • Avoid redundancy in your PPE. For example, hsap>=1 is equal to hsap=1T, so no need to mention them twice.
  • Merge different PPE units for faster execution. For example hsap=1T AND mmus=1T can be merged as hsap+mmus=2T.

The PPE Grammar in Detail

Individual grammatical units of PPE expressions are composed of two parts:

  1. A taxa specification. This can be any one of:
    • a species abbreviation (e.g. tgon)
    • a clade abbreviation (e.g., BACT for all Eubacteria taxa)
    • a list of species or clade abbreviations linked by plus sign "+" (e.g. tgon+pfal+hsap+FIRM).
    • ALL to represent all taxa in OrthoMCL.
  2. A logical comparison operator followed by a count.
    • operators allowed are: >, <, =, >=, and <=
    • the count is either:
      • a number, such as 5. This is a count of sequences that the operator applies to.
      • a number with a T, such as 5T. This is a count of taxa that the operator applies to.

Multiple expression units may be combined using AND or OR, and may use parentheses to provide explicit execution ordering.

tables.name: Sequences
tables.description:
This section features a Clustal Omega alignment tool (max 1000 sequences) and a tree visualization of proteins in this group. The proteins can be filtered in a number of ways,
  • Filter via text search on any/specific columns in the table.
  • Select one or more Pfam domains from the Pfam filter.
  • Restrict to Core Only, Peripheral Only or Core & Peripheral using the dropdown filter.
  • Filter taxonomically using the Organism filter.
The tree visualization is automatically updated with each selection. To run a Clustal Omega alignment after proteins are selected, choose the ‘Output format’ below the Protein List table and click the ‘Run Clustal Omega for selected genes’ button.

tables.name: SimilarGroup
tables.description: Similar groups are computed by a Diamond BLASTX comparison of the Representative Sequences (centroids) of all groups with each other. Groups with pairwise BLAST scores better than 1e-5 are considered similar.

tables.help: Group Statistics are a measure of cohesiveness for the proteins in an orthogroup. A pairwise BLAST e-value is computed between each protein and the Representative Sequence, which is the centroid of the group. A tight group will have a highly significant median of these pairwise e-values and also a significant maximum e-value (ie. less than 1e-10, since smaller e-values are more significant). The maximum e-value is a measure of the distance between the most dissimilar protein compared to the Representative Sequence.
tables.name: GroupStat
tables.description: Group Statistics are a measure of dispersion for an orthogroup. E-values are computed between all of the proteins vs. a central protein in the group.
